newsitem.title: CANADA: Market applauds Northstar, Morrison deal.
newsitem.headline: Market applauds Northstar, Morrison deal.

text.p: Investors on Friday hailed a planned merger between Northstar Energy Corp and Morrison Petroleums Ltd, driving up both oil and gas companies' stock prices in heavy volumes.
The two firms on Thursday announced a C$700-million friendly merger that came on the heels of a failed hostile takeover attempt for Morrison by Canadian 88 Energy Corp.
Morrison's stock climbed 0.45 to 10.35 by mid-session in Toronto with 3.6 million shares changing hands.
Northstar rose 0.65 to 14.80 on volume of 2.8 million shares. The companies announced the deal after Thursday's trading session.
Under the deal, each Morrison share would be exchanged for 0.7 of a Northstar share, which would give holders of both firms about equal representation in the merged company.
The merged C$1.3-billion company, which would have little debt, would then buy back about C$325 million of shares.
Company officials said Northstar and Morrison share close operations in four major oil and gas production areas in Alberta.
Combined output of the new Northstar would be about 42,500 barrels of oil equivalent per day, they said.
"It's definitely positive for Morrison shareholders and the stock's up nicely," Peter Linder, analyst with brokerage CIBC Wood Gundy said. "They're merging with a quality company."
The firms, which would combine much of their management teams, said they planned to continue with the bulk of exploration and production plans that were hatched as separate entities.
That included Morrison's much-watched deep natural gas exploration in the foothills of southwestern Alberta, which was seen as a key to Canadian 88's advance.
